Title: 10.40.400 Improve assets
Description:
In Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Process 10.40.400 – Improve assets is part of the Acquire to Dispose asset lifecycle under Manage fixed assets.

✅ What it means:

This process refers to capital improvements or enhancements made to existing fixed assets after acquisition. These improvements increase the asset’s value, extend its useful life, or enhance its functionality, and must be accounted for correctly.

🔍 Typical activities in this process:

  1. Identify improvement costs

    • Costs related to upgrades, major repairs, or modifications that meet capitalization criteria (not routine maintenance).

  2. Create an asset transaction

    • In D365 FO, you record the improvement as an acquisition adjustment or capitalization transaction against the existing asset.

  3. Update asset value and depreciation

    • The system recalculates depreciation based on the new adjusted value and remaining useful life.

  4. Compliance and audit trail

    • Ensure improvements are properly documented and posted to the correct ledger accounts.

Title: Ability to manage coverage time fence
Description: Cerro will apply coverage groups to manage time fences as part of the planning process. The specific values will be finalized during design sessions. The purpose of a coverage time fence is to filter out 'noise' created by planning suggestions for requirements that are far in the future (e.g., forecasts for next year or customer orders placed beyond typical lead times). A coverage time fence is defined as the number of days from the current planning date during which supply and demand are excluded. To prevent planning delays, the coverage time fence must be set longer than the total lead time for the item. Example : Shelbina plans - 3 Weeks ahead.

Title: Ability to group firmed orders by vendor

Title: Ability to assign vendor for a planned purchase order based on trade agreements

D365 will leverage trade agreements to identify the most suitable vendor based on parameters such as minimum lead time or lowest unit price. The selected vendor will be automatically populated on the planned purchase order to ensure consistency and efficiency in sourcing.

Title: Ability to manage receipt margin when generating planned purchase orders
Description: D365 SCM will support setup of receipt margins for planned purchase orders. Receipt margin defines the buffer time (in days) added after the requirement date. Master Planning will calculate an adjusted receipt date by applying this margin, ensuring suppliers deliver before the actual demand date and reducing supply risks.

Title: Ability to manage reorder margin when generating planned purchase orders
Description: D365 SCM will support setup of reorder margins for planned purchase orders. Reorder margin provides a time buffer (in days) before the item lead time, applied during Master Planning. Users will have the ability to override the default lead time by adjusting delivery dates when firming planned orders, ensuring realistic and executable purchase schedules.

These Legal Entities moving forward in D365 will be amalgamated into one legal entity with multiple sites. There will be 4 Sites in D365 F&SCM. Plus additional sites for customers (HD warehouses) consignment.

Title: Ability to define and maintain Warehouses
Description: Warehouses are usually a geographic location. In some cases, we can have virtual warehouses, as an exception. A Site can have multiple Warehouses. The Warehouse types could be Default (Main) , Quarantine, Transit. The structure of Warehouse will be defined during the Design phase.

Title: Ability to define and maintain locations
Description: Location is the most specific indication of where the items are stored in the warehouse. Location can have the characteristics of - Aisle, - Rack, - Shelf and - Bin position. Also they can be of types - Bulk, - Picking , - Staging,- Production Input, - Production Output, - Inbound Dock, - Outbound Dock , - Inspection Etc.  Using locations support determining pick routes, counting operations, and other decisions based on the locations where the items are stored. Cerro Warehouse team with appropriate privileges will be able to create and Maintain Locations.

Title: Ability to define Fixed location for MRO items
Description: Cerro requires the ability to create and assign fixed warehouse locations for MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Operations) items to ensure consistent storage and easy retrieval.

Title: Ability to group Warehouse locations by Zones
Description: Warehouse Zone is a logical grouping of locations within a warehouse. Zones help organize areas based on handling requirements, or any operational criteria. This functionality can be set in D365 F&SCM to simplify Work templates and Location directives Ex: - Put-away directives: tells the system to store received goods in a specific zone. - Picking directives: limits Picking work to certain zones for efficiency.

Title: Ability to manage PROX payment terms
Description:
The system must correctly calculate due dates for invoices using Prox payment terms to ensure accurate AR aging and reporting.

Prox payment terms are used by a specific group of customers/vendors, primarily affiliated distributor buying group customers. 

Currently, approximately:

  • 25+ customers under the LineSet business unit
  • 25+ customers under the Plumbing business unit

These customers generate quite a large volume of invoices, making manual due date entry impractical.

In AX 2012, Prox payment terms are not calculated correctly. 

This results in:

  • Incorrect invoice due dates
  • Inaccurate AR aging reports
  • Misclassification of invoice balances into incorrect aging buckets

Currently, Michelle manually adjusting due dates and amounts at the report level to produce accurate aging reports. These adjustments do not correct the underlying transactional data.


Business Requirement:
The system must implement the correct Prox payment terms logic for due date calculation and ensure that both transactional data and reporting reflect accurate due dates.

Prox Terms Calculation Logic:

  • If an invoice date falls on or before the 25th of a month, the due date must be the 10th of the following month.
  • If an invoice date falls after the 25th of the month, it must be included in the next cycle.

Examples:

  • February 26 – March 25 > Due April 10
  • March 26 – April 25 > Due May 10

Success Criteria:

  • AR aging reports reflect accurate due dates and aging buckets.
  • No manual correction is required to produce accurate aging.
  • Underlying invoice data matches reported values.

Title: 65.60.400 Analyze customer risk
Description:
In Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Process 65.60.400 – Analyze customer risk is part of the Order to Cash process under Manage credit and collections.

✅ What it means:

This process focuses on assessing the financial risk associated with customers to minimize bad debt exposure and ensure healthy cash flow. It’s about evaluating creditworthiness and monitoring ongoing risk.

🔍 Typical activities in this process:

  1. Credit Limit Review

    • Analyze customer credit limits based on historical payment behavior, outstanding balances, and aging reports.

  2. Risk Scoring

    • Use internal metrics (payment history, overdue invoices) and external data (credit bureau reports) to assign risk scores.

  3. Collections Analysis

    • Review overdue accounts and collection trends to identify high-risk customers.

  4. D365 FO Tools

    • Credit and collections workspace for dashboards.
    • Credit limit alerts and workflows for approvals.
    • Customer aging reports and Power BI integration for predictive analytics.

Title: 65.60.500 Analyze revenue

✅ What it means:

This process focuses on reviewing and interpreting revenue data to understand trends, customer contribution, and overall financial performance. It’s about turning raw revenue figures into actionable insights for decision-making.

🔍 Typical activities in this process:

  1. Collect Revenue Data

    • Pull data from Sales orders, Invoices, and General Ledger.
    • Include breakdowns by product, region, customer segment, and time period.

  2. Perform Analysis

    • Compare actual vs. forecasted revenue.
    • Identify top customers and revenue concentration risk.
    • Spot seasonal trends or anomalies.

  3. Use D365 FO Tools

    • Financial reporting (Management Reporter) for revenue statements.
    • Power BI integration for dashboards and advanced analytics.
    • Customer aging and credit reports for correlation with revenue patterns.

  4. Generate Insights

    • Highlight growth opportunities or declining segments.
    • Support pricing, discount strategies, and credit risk decisions.

Description:
Auto-Pay Method of Payment

Setup & Configuration in D365FO

Overview

The Auto-Pay method of payment leverages D365FO's Promissory Note functionality to automate the vendor payment process at the time of invoice posting. When configured, the system will automatically generate and post a Draw Promissory Note journal upon posting a vendor invoice, effectively settling the invoice and recording the payment against the designated bank account — without requiring a separate manual payment run.

Configuration Steps

Step 1: Create a Journal Name for Auto-Pay

Navigate to General Ledger > Journal Setup > Journal Names and create a new journal with the following settings:

Field

Value

Journal Name

e.g., AUTOPAY

Description

Auto-Pay – Vendor Draw Promissory Note

Journal Type

Vendor draw promissory note

Voucher Series

Assign an appropriate number sequence

 

📝 Note: The journal type 'Vendor draw promissory note' is specifically designed to create a promissory note liability and settle it against the vendor invoice in a single automated step.

Step 2: Configure the Auto-Pay Method of Payment

Navigate to Accounts Payable > Payment Setup > Methods of Payment and create or modify a method of payment:

Field

Value

Method of Payment

e.g., AUTO-PAY

Description

Auto-Pay (Automatic Draw Promissory Note)

Period

Invoice (one payment per invoice) or Total (one payment per vendor)

Account Type

Bank

Payment Account

Select the designated bank account

Draw Journal Name

Select the journal name created in Step 1 (e.g., AUTOPAY)

 

Under the Auto-Pay settings on the method of payment:

  • ✅ Enable Auto-Pay — Set to Yes
  • ✅ Create and post draw promissory note journal automatically — Set to Yes

 

This configuration tells D365FO that when an invoice is posted for a vendor assigned this method of payment, the system should automatically create and post the draw promissory note journal, which settles the invoice and records the bank payment in one seamless step.

Step 3: Assign the Method of Payment to the Vendor

Navigate to Accounts Payable > Vendors > All Vendors, select the applicable vendor(s), and update:

Field

Value

Method of Payment

AUTO-PAY

Bank Account

Ensure the vendor's bank account is set up (if applicable for electronic remittance)

 

💡 Tip: All new invoices created for this vendor will inherit the AUTO-PAY method of payment by default.

End-to-End Process Flow

1.      Pending Vendor Invoice Created

A vendor invoice (PO-based or Non-PO) is entered through the Pending Vendor Invoices form.

2.      Invoice Validated & Approved via Workflow

The invoice is submitted through the configured vendor invoice approval workflow for review and approval.

3.      Invoice Posted

Upon workflow approval, the invoice is posted, recording the AP accrual (Debit: Expense/Inventory/Asset; Credit: Accounts Payable).

4.      Auto-Pay Triggers Automatically

Because the vendor's method of payment is set to AUTO-PAY, D365FO automatically creates and posts a Draw Promissory Note journal.

5.      Invoice Settled & Bank Payment Recorded

The draw journal settles the vendor invoice (Debit: Accounts Payable; Credit: Bank Account), clearing the vendor balance and recording the cash outflow.

Accounting Impact

The table below illustrates the accounting entries generated at each step of the Auto-Pay process:

Step

Debit

Credit

Invoice Posting

Expense / Inventory / Asset

Accounts Payable (Vendor)

Auto-Pay (Draw PN Journal)

Accounts Payable (Vendor)

Bank Account

 

The net result is that the vendor invoice is fully settled at the time of posting, and the cash outflow is immediately reflected in the bank account — eliminating the need for a separate payment proposal or payment journal run.

Key Benefits

  • Streamlined Processing — Eliminates the manual step of creating a separate payment journal and running a payment proposal for auto-pay vendors.
  • Real-Time Settlement — Invoice and payment are recorded simultaneously, keeping vendor balances current.
  • Immediate Bank Impact — Payment is booked to the bank at invoice posting, providing accurate cash position visibility.
  • Audit Trail — The draw promissory note journal provides a clear, traceable link between the invoice and the payment.

Design Considerations

  • Vendor Scope — Identify which vendors should be assigned the Auto-Pay method of payment (e.g., utility companies, recurring service providers, intercompany vendors, or vendors with EFT/direct debit arrangements).
  • Workflow Approval — Since payment is automatic upon invoice posting, ensure the vendor invoice workflow includes appropriate approval steps before posting to maintain internal controls and SOX compliance.
  • Bank Reconciliation — Auto-pay transactions will appear on the bank statement and should be reconciled through the standard bank reconciliation process (or Advanced Bank Reconciliation if configured).
  • Segregation of Duties — Consider who has access to post vendor invoices with the Auto-Pay method, as posting the invoice effectively triggers a payment.

Title: Ability to set default system date for AJEs
Description:
n D365 Finance & Operations, “Ability to set default system date for AJEs” refers to a feature that allows you to control what date is automatically populated when creating Adjusting Journal Entries (AJEs)—typically during period-end or year-end close.

✅ What it means:

  • By default, D365 FO uses the current system date when you create a new journal line.
  • This feature lets you override that default and set a specific date (e.g., the last day of the fiscal period) for all AJEs, so users don’t have to manually change the date for every entry.

🔍 Why it’s useful:

  • Consistency: Ensures all adjusting entries post to the correct period.
  • Efficiency: Reduces manual errors and saves time during close.
  • Compliance: Helps meet accounting standards for cutoff dates.

⚙️ How it works:

  • Typically configured in General Ledger parameters or Journal setup.
  • You can define:
    • A fixed date (e.g., 31-Dec-2025).
    • Or allow users to select a default date when opening the journal.

90.70.005 Audit financial transactions
Description:
In Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Process 90.70.005 – Audit financial transactions is part of the Record to Report process area, specifically under Manage compliance and internal controls.

✅ What it means:

This process focuses on reviewing and validating posted financial transactions to ensure they comply with accounting standards, internal policies, and regulatory requirements. It’s about internal audit and control, not external statutory audit.

🔍 Typical activities in this process:

  1. Transaction Review

    • Examine posted vouchers, journal entries, and subledger details for accuracy.
    • Check for proper approvals and segregation of duties.

  2. Compliance Checks

    • Validate adherence to GAAP/IFRS or local accounting standards.
    • Ensure tax and reporting rules are correctly applied.

  3. Exception Reporting

    • Use D365 tools like Audit Workbench, Financial Period Close Workspace, and Security/Workflow logs to identify anomalies.

  4. Documentation & Evidence

    • Maintain audit trails for all corrections and approvals.
    • Prepare reports for internal or external auditors.

Why it matters:

  • Strengthens internal controls.
  • Reduces risk of fraud or misstatement.
  • Supports regulatory compliance and smooth external audits.

Thanks for raising this. Let me clarify the intent and the impact.

The BAI2 file delivery from BOA is not part of the EDI background jobs. This is a bank statement integration used specifically for the Bank Reconciliation module in D365, and it follows a different pattern than the EDI/AS2 workflows used for trading partner transactions.

The plan is:

  • BOA sends the BAI2 file via AS2

  • The file is dropped into a SharePoint location

  • D365 users manually import the file through the Bank Reconciliation workspace

This is a standard approach for BAI2 ingestion when a fully automated bank statement integration is not in scope.

Regarding SharePoint: If the organization is already evaluating SharePoint licensing for the P&R IT initiative, this requirement aligns well with that direction. The BAI2 drop‑off location would simply be another controlled SharePoint folder, so it does add weight to the business case but does not introduce additional architectural complexity.

Axiamatic-Risk Tracking: Testing vs Execution Gaps
Description:
Tracking testing vs execution in an axiomatic way gives architects dual assurance:

  • System is right — requirements are correctly implemented, with no gaps in logic.

  • System is ready — users and processes are aligned, reducing post‑go‑live surprises and accelerating stabilization.


Example in Vendor Creation (D365 F&O)

Requirement : All new vendors must be approved by the Procurement Manager before they can be activated for transactions.

Test Case (Axiomatic Testing)

  • QA team validates in ADO that when a new vendor record is created, its status remains Pending Approval until the Procurement Manager approves.

  • Edge cases tested:

    • Vendor created with incomplete mandatory fields (system should block).

    • Vendor created with all fields complete but without approval (system should prevent PO creation).

  • Test case IDs linked to the requirement for traceability.

Execution Scenario (CRP2)

  • Business users simulate creating a new vendor in CRP2 with sample data.

  • Procurement Manager receives approval notification, reviews vendor details, and activates the vendor.

  • End-to-end flow validated: vendor creation → approval → vendor activation → PO creation.

Architect View (Tracking & Risk)

  • Dashboard shows:

    • Requirement covered by test case 

    • Requirement validated in CRP2 scenario 

  • If either is missing:

    • Testing gap → risk of hidden workflow defect (e.g., vendors bypassing approval).

    • Execution gap → risk of poor adoption or delays in vendor onboarding.

Provides a clear view of risks at architect level:

  • High Risk: No test + no execution scenario.

  • Medium Risk: Test exists but not executed in CRP2.

  • Low Risk: Both test and execution validated.

Title: (COMEX) Ability to manage Sales orders with Commodity pricing - Release 2
Description:
Sales Order Pricing at Cerro is governed by the following key variables:

1. COMEX - A commodity exchange benchmark monitored by both Procurement and Sales.
2. PMA (Prior Month Average) - Uses the average closing price from the previous calendar month instead of the current day’s COMEX rate.
3. CPMV (Cerro Published Metal Value) - Updated monthly.
4. Multiplier - A customer-specific factor, determined and maintained by Sales.

In D365 - Masters / Config / logic needs to be built: 

1. A master data framework is required to configure and maintain commodity pricing.
2. A potential subscription feed from the COMEX site may be leveraged to capture intraday values. Currently the Comex Price is captured manually and the plan is to interface with the COMEX site to get the daily price. The integration needs to be discussed. It was also discussed during the requirement gathering sessions that the current fields needs to be evaluated and only the fields needed are to be carried forward. 3. Master tables will be managed by authorized Cerro personnel, with role-based security to be configured.               4. Custom tables with data entities will be required to support migration of historical and reference value.
 5. Once commodity values are established in D365 F&SCM, custom logic must populate the relevant variables automatically in the Sales orders. These values will be referenceable on the Sales order and can be applied to the Sales order line.
6.Cerro would need the ability to calculate the Comex Prior Month Average based on the Comex prices in D365
7.Cerro users with appropriate privileges would need the ability to set / update the Customer specific multipliers that will be applied on a Sales order.
8.Cerro users will need the ability to select daily, fixed, or prior month average COMEX pricing for different customers and orders is required. These selections must drive reporting (spread/KPIs) only and must not affect the actual invoice price in D365.

Notes: This is an existing customization in AX 2012. Reviewed with business and will be optimized for D365.

    • Functional defect

    • Data issue
    • Environment issue
    • Configuration gap
    • Dependency on upstream process
    • Out of scope / design confirmation needed

Reporting & Dashboard Visibility

  • ✅ Failed test cases must display associated failure reasons
  • ✅ Dashboard must support:
    • Count of partially completed failures
    • Failure reason categorization
  • ✅ Users can drill down from dashboard to:

Title: AP Invoice Workflow
Description:
We need to have a validation Workshop on AP Invoice Workflows before CRP4.
PO Workflows with DOA are currently in place. The PO workflow is a strong upstream control to ensure pricing, vendor, and quantities are approved before the commitment is made.
The AP invoice is not just a repetition of the PO, it is the financial recognition event, where actual liabilities are recorded. That introduces a different control requirement.
We can recommend and design a conditional workflow that only triggers when needed. Only exceptions are reviewed, which is where the real risk lies.
  • Price variance
  • Quantity variance
  • Missing receipt
  • Tolerance exceeded

When the workflow is routed for approval, the reviewer validates the exception before posting.
The WF History will have a clear audit trail showing that mismatches were reviewed and approved.
This approach —PO approval + conditional AP invoice workflow— is standard practice in D365FO and aligns with how most organizations balance automation with financial control.
We will schedule a validation Workshop to finalize this.

Marmon P&R Cerro — Inventory Costing Design Session

Date: 06/16/2026 | Type: Design / Blueprint Workshop

Organizer: Tiffany Hodges-Watson (HSO) | Led by: 

Ashley (Cerro)

Participants:  Joan Oruwari Nolan Keathley, Emily Hendrix (Marmon); Michelle Loewe, Marissa Snyder, Rick Perez (Cerro Flow)

 

Purpose

Finalize open costing decisions ahead of go-live, anchored to Key Decision ticket 7319 ("costing process for inventory transactions to be finalized"). The session focused heavily on how to handle Work-In-Process (WIP).

 

Key Topics Discussed

- Costing methodology — Confirmed weighted-average costing. Open challenge: deriving the opening inventory cost per item at go-live, since AX 2012 only holds a total GL balance (not segmented by item) plus a large Excel sheet.

- WIP definition — Clarified that WIP is a state, not a physical item; there is no true system WIP in D365 because Cerro back-flushes and ends production orders immediately. Real in-process material (extruded shells, coils, partially drawn tube) is tagged/weighed during twice-yearly counts.

- Finished goods & raw materials — Straightforward: copper metal value (~$5.937/lb) extrapolated against on-hand pounds/pieces from AX. Only metal value is in scope; the labor/overhead "fab component" is maintained separately.

- Costing by site — Inventory tracked by site (Sauget, Vinita Park, Shelbina, Mexico); costs differ by site, so opening balances load per site.

- Day-one vs. day-two approach — Day one: create and immediately end production orders (back-flush). Day two: introduce route operations with report-as-finished steps to capture true WIP.

 

Decisions Made

- Costing methodology = weighted average (confirmed).

- Create a new "WIP" item (e.g., item "W00019") to hold in-process value; add an extra extrusion/conversion step so production orders consume the WIP item instead of billets.

- WIP item posts to a dedicated manual WIP GL account, separate from the true system WIP account (1302-00), which should remain zero at go-live.

- GL mapping: billets/semi-finished → 1302-00-500 (SFG); opening balance → 1302-00-10; fab component maintained separately. In OneStream, SFG and WIP both roll into "working process."

- Three accounts Emily adjusts manually: fab-cost inventory, finished goods, and WIP (plus LIFO/FIFO entries).

- Manual WIP account to be blocked — corrections via inventory adjustment journals.

- Avoid the literal word "WIP" in the item name (audit concern); item number starts with "W."

- One WIP SKU at Sauget (avoid proliferation), since only metal cost matters.

- Load opening on-hand inventory as of month-end 5/31, pulled from InventTrans by SKU.

-  Cerro team — Produce per-item inventory cost by site; provide on-hand by SKU as of 5/31. Target: Fri, June 19.

- Cerro / HSO — Create the new WIP item(s) in data migration; update BOMs to consume WIP instead of billets; configure the manual WIP GL account.

- Emily — Check Craig's availability; reschedule a follow-up (Craig needed for LIFO/FIFO detail).

- Scrap costing — Deferred to a separate meeting (not yet aligned).

- Replicate the WIP solution at Shelbina and Vinita Park (no billets at Vinita Park — uses MES, which complicates the true-WIP account); Mexico has no WIP concern.

 

Risks / Blockers

- Timeline — Volume of open decisions is pushing go-live out; July and September vacations affect availability; the June 19 target is tight.

- Data accuracy — Extrusion/WIP pounds are manually tracked on paper and rolled forward monthly (miscount risk).

- Scrap valuation — Unresolved; flagged as a potential cost-distortion issue.

- MES at Vinita Park/Shelbina — Feeds the WIP account during the day but not for items not yet put away, creating reconciliation gaps.

These tables/logic should be incorporated in the underlying scripts. These static tables should only be for mappings or consolidations. There should be documentation around what are the steps to get to the final dataset ready for migration. The manual steps should be as minimal as possible so when running the later cycles the requried migration dataset can be prepared as quickly as possible.

Title: Sauget CW Items Sales UOM requirement
Description:
Hi Nolan,

Summarizing the call and the changes :


Scenario :

  • SO created for Sauget ,Catch Weight Item Ex: ¾ L 60
  • Item will be sold in Ft
  • Unit conversion set for the item ea->ft 1 ea = 60 ft
  • CW qty will be entered Ex: 100 ea
  • Expected calculation 100 ea = 6000 ft
  • D365 calculation 5976.50 ea is based on the standard function looping through (ea↔lb, lb↔ft, ea↔ft)
    • 100 ea × 25.0714 lb/ea = 2507.14 lb
    • 2507.14 lb × 2.38379 ft/lb = 5976.50 ft
  • We had a higher variance in the Sales Qty during the testing due to three conversion factors (ea↔lb, lb↔ft, ea↔ft) were provided independently and don't mathematically reconcile with each other , each pair was rounded/entered on its own rather than derived from a single base conversion.
    • Value provided 1 lb = 2.38379 ft . Expected value to 1 lb = 2.393164 ft (the exact inverse of 1 ft = 0.417857 lb entry).

Requirement:

  • Need a flag or method to define the fixed unit conversion from ea->ft .
    • Note: The “SEC” AX 2012 Customization on the item master was descoped earlier per discussion with Nolan and was later introduced as a calculation field only.
  • Use the flag - each to feet direct conversion method.
    • In AX 2012 this is a fixed value on the Item master independent of the UOM conversions
  • This change is applicable for all CW items in Sauget where the flag is set

Confirmed by the team :

  • Ea Units , Item list prices for Reefer coils are working as expected and the pricing is correct
  • Item list price will be set if sold in multiple UOM as an industry standard
We are moving forward with the change. Please let me know if I have missed anything .

You have already identified a workaround for this behavior. Another option I tested is to create a delivery address and assign it to the worker who creates the purchase requisition. Address selection hierarchy:

Item line = Warehouse > Site > Legal entity

Impact Analysis

1-) Impact on Data Migration

Approximately 60,000 expense items currently configured as non-stock items will need to be converted to stock items in Dynamics 365 to support warehouse receiving and put-away processes. Since these items should not carry inventory value on the balance sheet, they will be maintained as zero-cost inventory items. (expensed upon receipt)

The following master data updates will be required during data migration:

  • Item Model Group
    • Update the Item Model Group from the current non-stock configuration to "SI" (Stock Item).
  • Storage Dimension Group
    • Assign a new Storage Dimension Group appropriate for stocked items.
    • The final Storage Dimension Group value will be confirmed by Arun.
  • Procurement Category
    • The Procurement Category associations with these items established during CRP4 can remain unchanged.
    • Retaining these associations will continue to support purchasing classification and reporting.
  • Item Group
    • During CRP4, these items were assigned to the SVC (Services) Item Group because they were configured as non-stock items and therefore did not require inventory posting profiles.
    • As these items will now become stocked items, appropriate inventory posting definitions are required.
    • New Item Groups should be created based on the business-approved categorization (aligned with Procurement Categories where appropriate).
    • Corresponding General Ledger posting profiles must be configured for each new Item Group before migration in GOLD env.
The Business SME (Beth) will provide the final list of items that will remain under Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI). These items will also be included in this conversion. However, to enable separate tracking and reporting, they will be classified under a distinct Group.

2-) Financial and Inventory Validation

Because these items will now generate inventory transactions while remaining financially expensed through a zero-cost inventory model, validation of the accounting behavior is required.

Prior to UAT, preferably following the first successful data migration iteration, a working session should be conducted with the business stakeholders to validate:

  • General Ledger postings generated for purchasing and inventory transactions.
  • Zero-cost inventory behavior.
  • Inventory transaction creation and tracking.
  • Warehouse receiving and put-away process using warehouse locations, especially to validate the put-away location in the receiver document.
  • Confirmation that no unintended inventory valuation impacts occur on the balance sheet.

Business sign-off should be obtained before proceeding to UAT.

3-) Beginning Inventory Balances (Cutover)

As part of cutover activities, beginning inventory quantities will need to be loaded into D365 for the converted stock items.

Key considerations include:

  • Beginning inventory will be migrated with on-hand quantities only and zero inventory cost.

The 1430 account is the Prepayment account, and it's also included in the Vendor Posting Profile in AP. That's why the report includes it when comparing the GL and subledger for reconciliation.

The prepayment process consists of three steps:

  1. Enter the prepayment invoice.
  2. Apply the payment against the prepayment invoice.
  3. Enter the final invoice and apply the prepayment.

Once all three steps are completed, the balance in account 1430 should be $0.00.

As shown in your screenshot, the -$20 / +$20 and -$20,000 / +$20,000 entries offset each other. However, the remaining $5 balance indicates that the prepayment has not yet been fully applied to the final invoice. Other saying, the final invoice has not been entered yet.

That's how this report should be interpreted. Alternatively, if you're performing a standard AP reconciliation, you can run the report filtered to the 2101 - AP Trade account only.

If the intent is to return the product to inventory and then have Quality inspect it before making a disposition decision, the product should be returned to stock first, moved to the appropriate inspection area, and then scrapped if necessary. This process is different from using a disposition code that immediately scraps the product upon receipt.

Title: Barcodes and Scanning of Finished Goods- IND
Description:
Marmon (IND) currently uses RF Smart integrated with Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 for scanning finished goods during warehouse outbound and shipping operations. As part of the D365 migration, this capability must be reproduced and improved.

  Steps for IND :

  1. Sales order created.
  2. Picking list generated from the sales order. Picking List Registration created with batch lines in Activated status.
  3. Batches are auto-reserved
  4. Warehouse coordinator reviews the picking list registration, cancels any lines with no batch reservation, prints the pick slip, and hands it to floor workers.
  5. Floor worker scans the pick list barcode on the pick slip using RF Smart → system loads all batch lines for that pick list.
  6. Floor worker scans each batch barcode (from BRICS packaging label on pallet) in any order → each scan updates the line status: Activated → Picked.
  7. When all batch lines are scanned, the system automatically sets the picking list registration to Completed — no manual post step required.
  8. Floor worker prints shipping labels from RF Smart (address, PO#, SPLR ID, part number as applicable). One label per pallet or box. Must be done before the packing slip is posted.
  9. The Post Packing Slip button is removed from the RF Smart workflow — not available to floor workers.

Description:

If you enter the Site and Warehouse at the PO header, the system will automatically default those values to all PO lines.
